author: raman118
body:
#### References to other Issues or PRs

Fixes #21616.

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

`SetExpr(Interval(2, oo)) + oo` returned a nested singleton set instead of `{oo}`. Remove the extra set wrapper from the positive- and negative-infinity addition handlers. Tests cover bounded and unbounded intervals in both operand orders.

#### Other comments

The regression failed before the fix. All 16 `SetExpr` tests, code-quality tests (6 passed), Ruff, and `bin/mailmap_check.py` passed.

#### AI Generation Disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) generated all changes in `sympy/sets/handlers/add.py` and `sympy/sets/tests/test_setexpr.py`.

#### Release Notes

<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* sets
  * Fixed interval addition with positive or negative infinity producing nested singleton sets in `SetExpr`.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

commits.message:
Fix nested singleton sets in interval infinity addition

Remove the extra set wrapper in both infinity addition handlers and cover bounded and unbounded intervals in both operand orders.

AI-generated changes by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra).

diff:
diff --git a/sympy/sets/handlers/add.py b/sympy/sets/handlers/add.py
index dbc8c2a100c4..0af265f2a799 100644
--- a/sympy/sets/handlers/add.py
+++ b/sympy/sets/handlers/add.py
@@ -38,13 +38,13 @@ def _(x, y):
 def _(x, y):
     if x.start is S.NegativeInfinity:
         return Interval(-oo, oo)
-    return FiniteSet({S.Infinity})
+    return FiniteSet(S.Infinity)
 
 @_set_add.register(Interval, NegativeInfinity)
 def _(x, y):
     if x.end is S.Infinity:
         return Interval(-oo, oo)
-    return FiniteSet({S.NegativeInfinity})
+    return FiniteSet(S.NegativeInfinity)
 
 
 @_set_sub.register(Basic, Basic)
diff --git a/sympy/sets/tests/test_setexpr.py b/sympy/sets/tests/test_setexpr.py
index 1ba4efef99fe..4bb726cba2f0 100644
--- a/sympy/sets/tests/test_setexpr.py
+++ b/sympy/sets/tests/test_setexpr.py
@@ -40,6 +40,15 @@ def test_Add_Mul():
     assert (SetExpr(Interval(0, 1))*2).set == Interval(0, 2)
 
 
+def test_interval_add_infinity():
+    cases = [(Interval(2, oo), oo), (Interval(-oo, 2), -oo),
+             (Interval(1, 2), oo), (Interval(1, 2), -oo)]
+    for interval, infinity in cases:
+        expr = SetExpr(interval)
+        assert (expr + infinity).set == FiniteSet(infinity)
+        assert (infinity + expr).set == FiniteSet(infinity)
+
+
 def test_Pow():
     assert (SetExpr(Interval(0, 2))**2).set == Interval(0, 4)
